canonical_name: Federal Decree-Law 10/2025 — Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorism Financing + Proliferation Financing
description: The UAE's primary federal AML/CTF/PF statute. Replaces Federal Decree-Law 20/2018 (in force from October 2018). In force 14 October 2025. Strengthens supervisory powers + sanctions, updates beneficial-ownership requirements, expands PF coverage, aligns with FATF standards (post-grey-list-exit period). Cabinet Resolution 134/2025 issued in parallel as executive regulations.

canonical_name: Cabinet Resolution 134/2025 — Executive Regulations of FDL 10/2025
description: Executive regulations operationalising FDL 10/2025: detailed CDD + EDD + PEPs + SAR + sanctions screening + record retention requirements; designated-persons scope; supervisory cooperation; specific sectoral rules. Replaces Cabinet Decision 10/2019 (executive regulations of FDL 20/2018).

Predecessor AML/CTF/PF statute. In force October 2018 to 13 October 2025. Replaced by FDL 10/2025. Historical context for legacy compliance + transitional matters; existing CBUAE + sectoral guidance largely continues to apply where not inconsistent with the new framework.

Licensing + supervision framework for fiat-backed stablecoin issuers + payment token service providers operating in onshore UAE. In force progressively from late 2024. Establishes minimum capital, reserves backing, redemption rights, custody, AML/CFT alignment with FDL 10/2025, technology-risk requirements. Distinct from VARA + DIFC + ADGM frameworks for non-stablecoin virtual assets.

Securities and Commodities Authority framework for crypto-asset activities classified as securities or commodities under SCA jurisdiction (onshore UAE, outside Dubai/VARA + DIFC + ADGM scope). Covers token issuance, trading platforms, custody. Updated 2024-2025 to align with FDL 10/2025 + international standards.

canonical_name: DFSA Rulebook (Conduct of Business + AML + Crypto Tokens)
description: Comprehensive DIFC regulatory framework. Conduct-of-Business module (COB), AML/CFT module (AML), Crypto Tokens regime (CTKN — covers DIFC-licensed crypto activity). DFSA operates under DIFC's common-law system. AML alignment with FATF + federal UAE framework but DIFC-specific rules apply.

canonical_name: ADGM FSRA Rulebook + Digital Asset Framework (amended 10 June 2025)
description: ADGM Financial Services Regulatory Authority rulebook. Covers banking, insurance, asset management, securities, digital assets. The Digital Asset Framework was substantially amended 10 June 2025: notification-based regime for certain virtual asset activities; express prohibitions on privacy tokens + algorithmic stablecoins; tightened custody + AML requirements. ADGM operates under common-law system.

Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority rulebooks. Comprehensive Dubai-level licensing regime for Virtual Asset Service Providers (excluding DIFC + onshore UAE). 7 activity categories — advisory + broker-dealer + custody + exchange + lending-borrowing + management-investment + transfer-settlement. Each with detailed compliance, capital, governance + AML rules. Regularly updated; the most comprehensive standalone VA-regulator framework globally.

canonical_name: Federal Decree-Law 45/2021 — Personal Data Protection Law (UAE PDPL)
description: Federal UAE data-protection law. In force 2 January 2022. GDPR-inspired but with UAE-specific features. UAE Data Office is the supervisory authority. Applies to onshore UAE; DIFC + ADGM operate their own DP regimes. Implementing regulations (Executive Regulations) still being finalised in stages — limited enforcement to date.

canonical_name: DIFC Data Protection Law No. 5 of 2020
description: DIFC data-protection law. Adequacy with EU GDPR + UK GDPR. In force 1 July 2020. Mature enforcement track record under DIFC Commissioner of Data Protection. Frequently regarded as the most GDPR-equivalent regime in the GCC.
ADGM data-protection law. In force 14 February 2021. Substantially aligned with GDPR. ADGM Office of Data Protection enforces. Mandatory breach notification, DPIA, DPO, international-transfer rules.

Modern UAE insurance regulation. Confirms CBUAE's role as integrated insurance supervisor (post-merger of the Insurance Authority into CBUAE in 2020). Sets capital, conduct, market-conduct, brokerage + intermediary rules. Aligned with international insurance standards.

canonical_name: UAE Federal Penal Code — anti-bribery offences
description: Active + passive bribery of public officials + private-sector bribery (Federal Decree-Law 31/2021 Penal Code Articles 234-249). Penalties up to 10 years' imprisonment + significant fines. Investigated + prosecuted by the Federal Public Prosecution + Federal Court system.

Modernised UAE competition law. Anti-competitive agreements + abuse of dominant position + merger control. Ministry of Economy + the Competition Regulation Committee enforce. Material divergence from prior 2012 framework — increased fine ceilings + clearer merger thresholds.

metadata.supervisor: Ministry of Economy + Competition Regulation Committee

description: Modern UAE federal labour law. In force 2 February 2022. Replaces FDL 8/1980. Multiple employment-type categories (full-time / part-time / temporary / flexible / shared / remote); end-of-service gratuity; non-discrimination; work permits + Emiratisation. DIFC + ADGM operate distinct employment laws.

Integrated central bank + financial supervisor + insurance authority + payment systems regulator (post-merger of the Insurance Authority in 2020). Supervises banks, finance companies, insurance, payment service providers, money exchange houses, hawala providers, stablecoin/payment token issuers. Primary AML/CTF/PF supervisor for the federal-licensed financial sector.

Onshore UAE securities + commodities + crypto-asset supervisor (outside DIFC + ADGM). Licenses + supervises capital-markets intermediaries, public companies, securities exchanges (Dubai Financial Market + Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange), crypto-asset activities classified as securities.

canonical_name: Executive Office of Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (EOCN)
description: Federal AML/CTF policy coordinator + lead for FATF engagement. Established after the UAE's grey-listing in 2022; instrumental in the UAE's October 2024 grey-list exit. Coordinates across CBUAE + SCA + Ministry of Justice + Ministry of Economy + sectoral supervisors.

Within CBUAE. Receives + analyses SARs/STRs via the goAML platform; disseminates intelligence to law enforcement (Federal Public Prosecution, Federal Customs Authority) + foreign FIUs via Egmont Group. Operational expansion following the UAE's grey-list exit.

DIFC's integrated financial-services regulator. Operates DIFC's common-law-based regulatory regime: banking, insurance, asset management, securities + derivatives, crypto tokens, conduct + AML/CFT. Independent from federal CBUAE / SCA. DIFC is a separate jurisdiction with its own courts + laws (DIFC Court of First Instance + Appeal Court).

ADGM's integrated financial-services regulator. Operates ADGM's common-law-based regulatory regime: banking, insurance, asset management, securities, digital assets (significantly expanded), AML/CFT. Independent from federal CBUAE / SCA + from DIFC DFSA. ADGM is a separate jurisdiction (ADGM Courts).

Dubai-level dedicated VASP regulator. Established March 2022. Licenses 7 categories of virtual-asset services (excluding DIFC + onshore UAE-supervised activities). The most comprehensive standalone VASP regulator globally. Operates under Dubai's local emirate-level authority.

Federal data-protection regulator established under FDL 45/2021. Supervises PDPL compliance across onshore UAE (excluding DIFC + ADGM). Executive regulations still being finalised in stages — enforcement track record is limited.

DIFC's data-protection authority. Independent regulator under DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020. Active enforcer with mature track record; among the most GDPR-equivalent supervisory regimes in the GCC. Adequacy recognised with EU + UK.
ADGM's data-protection authority. Independent regulator under ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021. Operates under common-law jurisdiction; adequacy recognised with EU + UK.

Federal ministry covering competition + consumer protection + economic policy + DNFBP AML supervision (real-estate agents, dealers in precious metals + stones, accountants, lawyers, corporate service providers outside the financial-sector supervisors).

metadata.type: Federal economic ministry + DNFBP AML supervisor

description: Investigates + prosecutes federal financial-crime offences: money laundering (FDL 10/2025), terrorism financing, bribery (Penal Code), fraud. Federal Courts adjudicate; Court of Cassation as supreme appellate court.

canonical_name: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE)
description: Federal labour + employment regulator. Administers FDL 33/2021 labour law + work-permit regime + Emiratisation quotas + dispute-resolution framework. Onshore UAE only; DIFC + ADGM operate their own employment regulators (DIFC Employment + ADGM Employment Regulations).

Captures Financial Institutions (regulated by CBUAE + SCA + DFSA + FSRA per their respective scopes) + Designated Non-Financial Businesses + Professions (DNFBPs — real-estate agents, dealers in precious metals + stones, lawyers + notaries + accountants, corporate service providers, etc.) + VASPs (where regulated by CBUAE + SCA + DFSA + FSRA + VARA per scope). Multi-regulator architecture; same federal substantive obligations apply across regulators.

CDD applied at relationship establishment, occasional transactions above threshold (AED 55,000 / ~$15,000), wire transfers above threshold, suspicion of ML/TF/PF, doubts about prior CDD adequacy. Measures: identify + verify customer + UBO using reliable independent sources; understand purpose + intended nature; ongoing monitoring. Risk-based intensity; reliance on third parties subject to conditions.

EDD for higher-risk situations: foreign + domestic + IO PEPs (with risk-based assessment of domestic PEPs); high-risk jurisdictions (FATF + national identifications); complex / unusual / large transactions; correspondent banking; new products / technologies. Senior-management approval; SoW + SoF; enhanced ongoing monitoring; documented rationale. PEP family members + close associates within scope; 12-month tail after PEP function ends.

Identify + verify the beneficial owner of every customer (legal entity, legal arrangement, trust). 25% ownership / voting / control threshold + senior-managing-official fallback. UAE BO registry maintained by Ministry of Economy + sector-specific registries; FIs may access for CDD purposes. Particular focus on complex group structures + nominee arrangements.

Expanded PF obligations in FDL 10/2025 vs predecessor FDL 20/2018. PF risk assessment as a dimension of the entity-wide RBA; controls for UN-designated entities (DPRK + Iran focus); dual-use goods + sensitive-technology trade-finance scrutiny; sanctions-evasion typology training. Aligns with FATF R.1 + R.7 updates.

Designated persons must report to the FIU via the goAML platform without delay on knowledge or reasonable suspicion of ML / TF / PF or related predicate offences. Tipping-off prohibition. Statutory immunity for good-faith reports. The 2025 framework retains the predecessor reporting structure with operational + format updates.

Mandatory screening against UN Security Council Consolidated List + the UAE Local Terrorist List + targeted UAE-specific designations. Real-time customer + transaction screening; freeze + report regime; cooperation with EOCN-AML/CTF + Federal Public Prosecution. Continued operational focus following the UAE's October 2024 FATF grey-list exit.

canonical_name: FDL 10/2025 — Governance + AML compliance officer + training + retention
description: Documented written policies + procedures + senior-management approval; designated AML compliance officer (MLRO) at sufficient seniority + independence + resources; internal audit + compliance-function review; staff training proportionate to role + risk (incl. PF + sanctions typologies); record retention for at least 5 years after end of relationship or transaction.

Detailed operational rules under FDL 10/2025: prescribed CDD documentation; structured SAR content; specific PEP categorisation; risk-assessment minimum dimensions; transitional treatment of legacy relationships established under FDL 20/2018; supervisory reporting cadences + formats. Treated as the operational handbook by examiners.

Licensing for: payment token issuance (fiat-backed stablecoins denominated in AED or major currencies); payment token service provision (custody, exchange, transmission of payment tokens). Requirements: minimum capital, 100% reserve backing in high-quality liquid assets, daily reconciliation, redemption-at-par right, AML/CFT alignment with FDL 10/2025, technology-risk management. Distinct regime from VARA + DIFC + ADGM crypto frameworks.

DIFC regulatory regime for crypto tokens. Recognised tokens + securities tokens regulated; comprehensive AML, custody, market-conduct + technology-risk rules. Regularly updated; high approval bar similar to ADGM FSRA. Distinct from federal CBUAE / SCA + VARA scope.

canonical_name: ADGM FSRA Digital Asset framework (amended 10 June 2025)
description: ADGM Digital Asset framework substantially amended on 10 June 2025. Notification-based regime for certain virtual asset activities (faster market entry for established firms); express prohibitions on privacy tokens + algorithmic stablecoins; tightened custody requirements (cold-wallet + multi-party-computation expectations); MiCA-equivalent AML + market-conduct rules.

VASP licence required to provide any of: (1) Advisory services; (2) Broker-Dealer services; (3) Custody services; (4) Exchange services; (5) Lending + Borrowing services; (6) Management + Investment services; (7) Transfer + Settlement services. Each category has detailed rulebook: capital, governance, technology, AML, conduct + market-conduct requirements. Cross-category licensing common.

VARA prohibits: privacy tokens (Monero, Zcash, similar); algorithmic stablecoins (post-Terra collapse); anonymity-enhancing mixers / tumblers; specific high-risk DeFi structures. Quarterly review + supplement. Aligned with ADGM FSRA prohibitions but distinct legal authority.

canonical_name: UAE Local Terrorist List + designated entities
description: UAE-maintained list of designated terrorist organisations + supporters. Cabinet Resolution publication. Supplements UN Consolidated List for AML/CFT screening + asset-freeze obligations. Distinct from OFAC / OFSI / EU national lists; UAE firms operating internationally must screen against multiple lists.

FIU UAE's secure online platform for SAR + STR filing. Structured XML / form-based submission; supports designated-persons reporting; intelligence-dissemination to law enforcement + foreign FIUs. Mandatory channel under FDL 10/2025 + Cabinet Resolution 134/2025.

canonical_name: UAE multi-regulator overlay — federal + DIFC + ADGM + VARA
description: Firms operating across multiple UAE jurisdictions face simultaneous regulatory regimes: (a) onshore UAE federal (CBUAE / SCA + EOCN AML); (b) DIFC (DFSA + DIFC DP); (c) ADGM (FSRA + ADGM DP); (d) Dubai-VARA (excluding DIFC). Each regime has its own conduct + AML + DP + custody rules. Cross-regulator coordination + program design is a distinct compliance discipline.

UAE was placed on FATF's increased-monitoring list (grey list) in March 2022 due to deficiencies in AML/CTF supervision + enforcement. Significant reforms 2022-2024 (incl. EOCN establishment, sectoral enforcement escalation, BO transparency, VASP supervision) led to October 2024 grey-list exit. FDL 10/2025 + CR 134/2025 are part of the post-exit consolidation phase.

canonical_name: DIFC Employment Law (DIFC Law No. 4 of 2021)
description: DIFC's standalone employment regime. Mandatory written contracts; end-of-service gratuity calculation; non-discrimination; whistleblower protection; restrictive covenants; cross-border employment. Independent from federal FDL 33/2021. DIFC Court enforcement.
ADGM's standalone employment regime. Substantially aligned with common-law employment practice. Independent from federal FDL 33/2021 + DIFC Employment Law. ADGM Court enforcement.

Under FDL 10/2025: UAE Government PEPs (federal-level officials, senior emirate-level officials, federal court judges, senior military / police, leadership of state-owned enterprises) assessed on a risk-sensitive basis — typically still triggering EDD for politically-significant positions. Family members + close associates within scope. Specific operational guidance via EOCN-AML/CTF advisories.

Mandatory wage payment via banking channels for onshore private-sector employees; cross-checked against the WPS; non-compliance leads to permit + sanction risk. Emiratisation: minimum-Emirati-employee quotas for private-sector firms above thresholds (UAE Nafis programme). Distinct compliance discipline operating alongside FDL 33/2021 labour law.

Following the 2022 FATF grey-listing, UAE supervisors materially escalated enforcement: CBUAE imposed AED 9.4m+ in AML-related fines in 2024 alone (vs near-zero pre-2022); DFSA + FSRA + VARA + SCA active enforcement; Federal Public Prosecution pursued high-profile financial-crime convictions. Post-exit consolidation continues; FDL 10/2025 explicitly enhances supervisor sanctions powers.

Crypto firms commonly face 4-way regulatory consideration: CBUAE (where activities involve fiat-backed payment tokens); SCA (where tokens classified as securities/commodities onshore); DFSA (for DIFC operations); FSRA (for ADGM operations); VARA (for Dubai operations excluding DIFC). Firms must determine which authority licenses each activity + coordinate compliance accordingly. The most complex multi-regulator overlap in the UAE financial system.
